meta.triageRationale: One additive port method (IssueOps.resolveIssueId with the GitHub adapter and the signature fixtures) and one use of it in the adoption path of ensureUnitIssueDetailed; three source files in one module, one obvious approach, the contract already proposed as AMD-315d510cb28100e2-11.

findings.premise: The proposed lookup and adoption linking address the recorded S4-1 outcome.
findings.evidence: S4-1 explicitly requests 'link adopted Story and Task issues in ensureUnitIssueDetailed'. The actual adoption branch records and returns the issue without linking; the proposed change targets that branch. Analyzer tools were unavailable, so verification used source and artifact reads. [files: docs/plans/s4-open-issues.md, src/workflow/tracker/unit-issue.ts]

findings.premise: Label adoption currently skips linking, whereas successful creation records failed links for retry.
findings.evidence: The adoption branch executes 'recordUnit(unit, adopted, now())' and immediately returns. The creation branch calls linkSubIssue and stores '{ parent: parentRef, childId: created.value.id }' on failure. The local-resolution branch invokes retryPendingLink. [files: src/workflow/tracker/unit-issue.ts]
findings.action: Retain the existing creation and local-resolution behavior.

findings.premise: The ref-to-id operation is new, and the existing linking operation consumes a numeric database id through the injectable gh runner.
findings.evidence: IssueOps has no resolveIssueId member. ghLinkSubIssue takes 'childId: number' and calls runGh with '-F', 'sub_issue_id=${childId}'. runGh uses the _exec seam configured by _setTrackerExecForTests. [files: src/workflow/tracker/port.ts, src/workflow/tracker/github.ts, src/workflow/tracker/github-adapter.ts]
findings.action: Implement the new lookup through the stated runner and adapter.

findings.premise: Recording adoption first can be followed by saving its failed link through the existing recordUnit behavior.
findings.evidence: recordUnit selects 'prior !== undefined && prior.issue === issue ? prior : ...'. After the initial adoption write, another recordUnit call for that issue ignores a supplied pendingLink. The design specifies linking 'after recordUnit' but does not specify changing this preservation rule or explicitly patching the record. Such reuse loses the retry marker, and subsequent local ensures skip linking. [files: src/workflow/tracker/unit-issue.ts, src/workflow/tracker/refs.ts]
findings.action: Specify an explicit pendingLink patch that preserves revision and extras, or change recordUnit's merge semantics. Test persistence after the initial adoption record already exists.

findings.premise: Existing parent-and-childId records remain readable without a data rewrite.
findings.evidence: UnitIssue currently stores '{ readonly parent: string; readonly childId: number }'. readTrackerMeta reads the JSON without transforming this field, and retryPendingLink links directly using pending.childId. Retaining that branch supports existing records. [files: src/workflow/tracker/refs.ts, src/workflow/tracker/unit-issue.ts]
findings.action: Keep the childId-first retry branch and the proposed legacy-record test.

findings.premise: The storage change is rollbackable after child-only records have been written.
findings.evidence: The old retry implementation unconditionally calls 'port.issueOps.linkSubIssue(pending.parent, pending.childId)'. A new '{ parent, child }' record supplies undefined after rollback; ghLinkSubIssue then submits 'sub_issue_id=undefined'. Forward compatibility with old records does not establish rollback compatibility. [files: src/workflow/tracker/unit-issue.ts, src/workflow/tracker/github.ts]
findings.action: State that rollback requires resolving or converting child-only records, or introduce a compatible reader before allowing those writes.

findings.premise: There are no HLD shared contracts or other Story ownership constraints to honor.
findings.evidence: AMD-315d510cb28100e2-11 declares 'type': 'sharedContract.methodAdd', 'contractId': 'sc1', and 'status': 'pending'. Its purpose says 'the GitHub adapter test is s1’s to add'. S4-1 names the prerequisite 's1 to agree; then link adopted Story and Task issues'. Standalone metadata does not remove that existing shared-contract dependency. [files: .insrc/artifacts/AMD-315d510cb28100e2-11.json, docs/plans/s4-open-issues.md, .insrc/artifacts/LLD-72b1bee074ba2dab-S001.json]
findings.action: Document the sc1 dependency and resolve the pending amendment and ownership before treating the port addition as an agreed contract.

findings.premise: The existing ref parser rejects every ref that is not owner/repo#N.
findings.evidence: parseIssueRef checks only the positions of '#' and '/'; it returns the remaining number string without validation. Values such as 'o/r#abc' and '/#' pass. github-adapter.ts explicitly notes: 'parseIssueRef alone only checks the separators' and uses a separate regex for assignee operations. [files: src/workflow/tracker/refs.ts, src/workflow/tracker/github-adapter.ts]
findings.action: Specify strict validation for ghGetIssueId and test malformed number and empty owner/repo components.

findings.premise: Using runGh and attempt yields only rejected or unreachable lookup failures.
findings.evidence: classifyGhFailure also returns 'missing-tool' for ENOENT and 'missing-signin' for authentication failures. The adapter's failure function preserves GhCommandError.kind. Thus the proposed implementation exposes more failure kinds than section 2.1 declares. [files: src/workflow/tracker/github.ts, src/workflow/tracker/github-adapter.ts, src/workflow/tracker/port.ts]
findings.action: Declare all PortFailureKind outcomes and apply the pending-link behavior to each.

findings.premise: The ac1 mapping covers every upstream acceptance criterion.
findings.evidence: The standalone artifact and repository searches yielded this LLD but no corresponding upstream Story acceptance-criteria artifact. S4-1 supplies an outcome, and existing unit-issue tests provide commitThenFail and failed-link retry fixtures, but they cannot establish that the synthetic ac1 exhausts upstream criteria. [files: .insrc/artifacts/LLD-72b1bee074ba2dab-S001.json, docs/plans/s4-open-issues.md, src/workflow/tracker/__tests__/unit-issue.test.ts]
findings.action: Define explicit acceptance criteria for Story and Task adoption, lookup/link retries, Epic exclusion, and legacy pending records, then map each to a specific test.

summary.prose: When a create times out after the tracker committed the issue, the next ensure finds it by its per-unit label and adopts it. Today an adopted Story or Task issue is never linked under its parent. This Story adds a ref-to-id lookup to the tracker's issue operations and uses it so the adopted issue is linked like a freshly created one; a lookup or link that fails is recorded and retried on the next ensure.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Link an adopted unit issue under its parent via resolveIssueId

api.name: IssueOps.resolveIssueId

parameters.name: ref
parameters.purpose: The issue whose tracker-internal numeric id is wanted, as 'owner/repo#N'.

returns.meaning: The issue's REST database id, the value linkSubIssue needs as childId.

errors.condition: The issue does not exist, gh fails or times out, or the response carries no numeric id.

preconditions: ref is a well-formed issue ref of the adapter's own owner and repo
postconditions: Reads only; nothing in the tracker changes

api.name: ghGetIssueId
api.signature: ghGetIssueId(owner: string, repo: string, ref: string): number

parameters.name: ref
parameters.purpose: Issue ref whose number is read.

returns.meaning: The issue's database id from `gh api repos/o/r/issues/N --jq .id`.

errors.condition: gh exits non-zero, or the output is not a positive integer.

postconditions: Runs through runGh, the same injectable exec seam as ghLinkSubIssue

api.name: ensureUnitIssueDetailed
api.signature: ensureUnitIssueDetailed(unit: UnitRef, port: TrackerPort, deps?: EnsureIssueDeps): EnsureResult<EnsuredIssue>

parameters.name: unit
parameters.purpose: The Story or Task (or Epic) unit.

errors.condition: A failed resolve or link on adoption never fails the ensure; it is recorded as pendingLink and logged.

preconditions: For a Story or Task unit the parent issue is already resolved (parentRef)
postconditions: An issue adopted by label under a known parent is either linked under it or carries a pendingLink on its record
An Epic adoption, and an adoption with no parent, make no link call

api.name: retryPendingLink
api.signature: retryPendingLink(unit: UnitRef, port: TrackerPort, issue: IssueRef): void

parameters.name: unit
parameters.purpose: The unit with a recorded pendingLink.

returns.meaning: Nothing; a link that still fails stays recorded.

postconditions: A pendingLink with childId links it; one with only `child` resolves the id first, then links; success clears pendingLink; any failure leaves it recorded

dataModelChanges.details: From { parent: string; childId: number } to { parent: string; childId?: number | undefined; child?: string | undefined }. childId is set when the id is known (a successful create, or a successful resolve); child (the issue ref) is set when the id could not be resolved, so the retry resolves it. At least one of the two is present. Records written before this change carry childId and stay valid.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff:
- pendingLink?: { parent: string; childId: number }
+ pendingLink?: { parent: string; childId?: number | undefined; child?: string | undefined }

dataModelChanges.details: Gains resolveIssueId (amendment AMD-315d510cb28100e2-11). Required on the type: the GitHub adapter and the compile-time signature fixture implement it; fakes that cast to TrackerPort need none.

errorCases.response: Treated as any rejected link: pendingLink is recorded and retried; no message matching, so the retry repeats until a person closes the loop

migration.stateBefore: An issue adopted by its per-unit label after a timed-out create is recorded and returned but never linked under its parent; the link and any pendingLink exist only for a create that succeeded (unit-issue.ts adoption branch, bundle c3). IssueOps has no way to read an issue's database id from its ref (bundle c2), and UnitIssue.pendingLink is { parent, childId }.
migration.stateAfter: IssueOps.resolveIssueId exists and the GitHub adapter implements it with gh api; the adoption branch resolves and links the adopted issue under its parent, recording pendingLink { parent, childId } or { parent, child } on failure; retryPendingLink resolves a child-only record before linking. pendingLink accepts either field.

migrationSteps.action: Add ghGetIssueId and the GitHub adapter's resolveIssueId, and declare resolveIssueId on IssueOps with the signature fixture updated

Widen the pendingLink type with an optional child ref and make childId optional; no stored record changes. Rolling back past this step requires every { parent, child } record to be resolved to a childId first (old code reads only childId and would send sub_issue_id=undefined)

Link on adoption in ensureUnitIssueDetailed and resolve first in retryPendingLink for a child-only record; rolling back leaves any { parent, child } record unreadable by old code, so resolve them to childId first

migration.backwardCompat: IssueOps gains a required member, so any full implementer outside this repository must add it; the only full implementers in the repository are the GitHub adapter, the compile-time fixture and the unit-issue fake. Stored pendingLink records written earlier carry childId and are read unchanged. The GitHub-facing behaviour for created issues is unchanged.

alternativesConsidered.name: IssueOps.resolveIssueId, link on adoption
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add resolveIssueId(ref) to IssueOps next to linkSubIssue and, when ensureUnitIssueDetailed adopts an issue by label under a known parent, resolve its id and link it, recording pendingLink on any failure.
alternativesConsidered.approach: IssueOps gains resolveIssueId(ref: IssueRef): PortResult<number>. The GitHub adapter implements it with one new gh wrapper, ghGetIssueId, that runs `gh api repos/o/r/issues/N --jq .id` through the same runGh seam as ghLinkSubIssue. In ensureUnitIssueDetailed, after recordUnit on the adopted issue, when parentRef is defined the call resolves the id and links it under the parent; if the resolve or the link fails, the existing UnitIssue.pendingLink { parent, childId } is stored (childId only when the id was resolved) and the existing retryPendingLink completes it on a later ensure. The signature fixture and the unit-issue fake gain the method.
pros: Matches the pending amendment AMD-315d510cb28100e2-11 exactly
Reuses recordUnit, pendingLink and retryPendingLink; no new record shape for the success path
Adoption and creation end with the same linked state
cons: A failed resolve has no childId to store, so pendingLink must allow an unresolved child or the retry must resolve first
Every full IssueOps implementer gains a required member

alternativesConsidered.name: Resolve inside linkSubIssue by ref
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Change linkSubIssue to accept an issue ref and resolve the id inside the adapter, so the unit code never handles ids.
alternativesConsidered.approach: linkSubIssue(parent, child: IssueRef | number) resolves a ref to its id inside the GitHub adapter and the unit-issue code passes the adopted ref. pendingLink stores the child ref instead of the id. No new port method is declared; the amendment is replaced by a signature widening.
pros: pendingLink becomes uniform: a ref is always known, even after a failed resolve
cons: Widens an approved port signature (a breaking change for implementers and the fixture) instead of the additive amendment already proposed
Changes the stored pendingLink shape, which needs a reader for old records with childId
Hides a second network call inside a method named link
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Widens an approved signature and changes the stored pendingLink shape for records already written; breaking where a1 is additive.

alternativesConsidered.name: Leave adopted issues unlinked, report them
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Do not link on adoption; surface an adopted-but-unlinked unit in the ensure result so a person links it.
alternativesConsidered.approach: ensureUnitIssueDetailed returns duplicateCheck/adopted information plus a linked:false flag on adoption and logs a warning; no port change. The link is left to the user or a later maintenance command.
cons: Leaves the defect S4-1 names in place: the Story or Task issue stays unlinked under its parent
Needs a manual step nobody owns
Does not satisfy the pending amendment
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Leaves S4-1 unfixed and depends on a manual step nobody owns.
